Mind-controlled humanoids could become home assistants

This is a genuinely promising use case for BCI+ humanoid robots.

China Mobile’s embodied intelligence team brought a humanoid robot with a dexterous hand to the Global Brain-Computer Interface × Medical Insurance Innovation Scenario Competition in China.

The team demonstrated brain-controlled grasping using a non-invasive BCI system.

A dexterous hand has multiple degrees of freedom and requires much more coordinated movement than a simple gripper. Translating brain signals into precise, timely, and stable hand movements is a significant challenge.

The team also used AR glasses instead of a separate external screen, making the interaction more wearable and potentially better suited to home rehabilitation.

Imagine the future...people with limited mobility could eventually use their own intentions to direct a humanoid robot to grasp objects and assist with everyday tasks.

Neuralink is already testing implantable brain-computer interfaces for tasks like controlling robotic arms to grasp objects or maneuvering wheelchairs...

it’s a truly wild and exciting future.

The king is in the house. And this is the end game. 

On SpaceX’s $SPCX first earnings call, Elon said it plainly: “We decided to go all-in on NVIDIA because the Vera Rubin architecture is the best. We are exclusive to Nvidia $NVDA .”

The space version is Starmind AI1: one satellite = one full Vera Rubin NVL72 rack (72 Rubin GPUs + 36 Vera CPUs, ~3,600 PFLOPS NVFP4, 20.7 TB HBM4, 120–150 kW). Cooling radiates into vacuum, solar is free. Prototypes early 2027, deployment Q4 2027, scale 2028. Built at Gigasat, Bastrop.

NVIDIA’s Space-1 Vera Rubin Module claims 25× the space inference of an H100. Jensen called space data centers with SpaceX “a particularly new market.”
On the ground: ~200k GB300s online per month. Next year shifts to Vera Rubin. Targets: 440k-GPU training cluster before Q2 2027, 10 GW incremental buildout in 2027.

Elon warned of stranded compute in half-built data centers. GPUs bought, power not connected. The “lock early, resell at 2–3×” model fails when the bottleneck is power, grid, cooling, and permitting — not the chip.

Ground centers hit power, cooling, and grid walls together. In orbit, sunlight is free and heat radiates into space. Earth isn’t out of room — it’s out of immediately usable room. Space is one of the fastest paths.

Superintelligence doesn’t start with parameter count. It starts when compute demand and supply enter a verified positive feedback loop — and that loop is only just beginning.

note_tweet.text:
Good morning @quipnetwork ☕️

I want to cover the quantum research result that I think is the single most important experimental finding for understanding the urgency of post-quantum security.

The 2023 IBM quantum error correction paper in Nature.

Not the Willow chip. Not the qubit count records. This specific paper. Here's why it changed how I think about the timeline.

The paper demonstrated a repetition code running on 127 physical qubits where the logical error rate decreased as the code distance increased.

That sentence requires unpacking because the implication is enormous.

Previous quantum error correction implementations shared a fundamental problem: as you added more qubits to improve error correction the overhead introduced new errors at roughly the same rate as the correction removed them. The net improvement was marginal. The scaling relationship was unfavorable.

The IBM Nature paper showed the relationship inverting.

More qubits. Better error correction. Net logical error rate going down as code distance goes up.

For the first time experimentally the error correction was winning against the noise.

Google's Willow result confirmed this a year later at larger scale and higher code distance. Two independent research groups. Two different hardware architectures. Same conclusion.

Quantum error correction scales favorably.

Here is the research implication stated as precisely as I can:

The engineering barrier that made fault-tolerant quantum computation seem perpetually 10 years away was the unfavorable scaling of error correction overhead. Every experimental result before 2023 suggested that noise grew faster than correction could compensate.

2023 and 2025 showed experimentally that this scaling relationship flips at sufficient code distance.

The barrier was real. Now it's been crossed. The path to fault-tolerant computation is open in a way it demonstrably was not before.

Shor's algorithm runs on fault-tolerant quantum hardware. The discrete logarithm problem the mathematical foundation of every wallet signature in crypto breaks on fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

The experimental confirmation that fault-tolerant scaling works changes the timeline from "theoretically possible but practically uncertain" to "engineering execution problem on a known trajectory."

Those are not the same thing.

My honest long view:

I read a lot of quantum research. Most results are incremental. Some are significant. A few are genuinely pivotal.

The favorable error correction scaling results from IBM and Google are pivotal. They are the experimental confirmation that the theoretical path to cryptographically relevant quantum computation is physically real rather than mathematically assumed.

Everything downstream of that confirmation @quipnetwork 's post-quantum wallets, the compute marketplace, the PoUW mechanism, the urgency of the airdrop window at https://t.co/5aKccd0qVp makes more sense when you understand what those papers actually proved.

The researchers updated their models in 2023. Most of CT hasn't updated theirs yet.

When did you last read a primary quantum computing research paper rather than a summary of one?

🚨 Et si le krach de la mémoire attendu en 2028 n’arrivait jamais ?

70–80 % de la surface de silicium d’un rack IA est de la mémoire. La HBM consomme 3 à 4 fois plus de wafers par Go que la DDR5.

Certaines actions mémoire cotent à 2x leurs leurs PE. Bernstein et SA en parle : 

Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis) et Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein) viennent de partager leurs perspectives sur l'industrie des semi-conducteurs au CASPA CEO Summit.

Plusieurs déclarations importantes pour les investisseurs.

1️⃣ Les véritables goulots :

Dylan Patel classe les contraintes industrielles dans cet ordre :

1/Substrats avancés, PCB et matériaux.
2/Mémoire HBM et DRAM.
3/Lasers et composants optiques.
4/Équipements et capacités de fabrication.
5/Électricité et infrastructures.

Il estime que près de 50 GW de data centers seront en construction dans le monde en 2027.

Mais fabriquer suffisamment de substrats avancés pourrait être beaucoup plus difficile que trouver de nouvelles solutions d'alimentation électrique.

🇹🇼 Unimicron (3037), Kinsus (3189) et Nan Ya PCB (8046) sont particulièrement bien positionnés sur ce marché.

2️⃣ Le supercycle de la mémoire pourrait durer bien plus longtemps que prévu.

Stacy souligne un paradoxe :

Certains fabricants de mémoire se négocient entre 2 et 4 fois leurs bénéfices prévisionnels.

La HBM nécessite environ 3 à 4 fois plus de wafers que la DDR5 conventionnelle pour produire une quantité équivalente de mémoire.

Les nouvelles salles blanches ne permettront d'augmenter significativement les capacités qu'en 2028-2029.

Le marché anticipe déjà un effondrement des prix de la DRAM en 2028.

Sa question : « Et si cela ne se produisait pas ? »

🇰🇷 SK hynix, Samsung et 🇺🇸 Micron pourraient maintenir des bénéfices exceptionnellement élevés plus longtemps qu'anticipé.

3️⃣ NVIDIA commence à perdre des parts de marché face aux ASIC.

Selon Dylan, NVIDIA consomme déjà une proportion décroissante des capacités mondiales de HBM et de CoWoS.

Google, Amazon et AMD gagnent du terrain.

Mais attention : NVIDIA pourrait continuer à doubler ses bénéfices malgré cette baisse de part relative.

4️⃣ Le véritable enjeu sera la répartition des marges.

Dylan estime que le coût d'un GW d'infrastructure IA est passé d'environ 40 Md$ en 2024 à plus de 60 Md$ en 2026.

Une part considérable de cette valeur est captée par NVIDIA et les autres concepteurs de puces.

Si les hyperscalers internalisent davantage leur conception, une partie des profits pourrait se déplacer vers les fournisseurs de mémoire, de substrats et de composants industriels.

🇹🇼 Pour les investisseurs taïwanais, cela renforce l'intérêt de TSMC, Unimicron, Kinsus et Nan Ya PCB.

Le marché IA peut continuer à exploser sans que NVIDIA conserve indéfiniment la même part de la valeur.

📅 2027-2028 : pénuries 
2029 : première véritable interrogation sur le risque de surcapacités.  
CASPA CEO Summit, 23 octobre 2026.

The stable and open international order erected on America’s watch is unraveling, argues CFR expert @CharlesKupchan. 

In his new book, Bringing Order to Anarchy: Governing the World to Come, Kupchan writes that democracy is losing ground to autocracy; globalized markets are fragmenting; and the era of perpetual peace foreseen at the close of the Cold War has given way to great-power rivalry.

What lies ahead is “a globalized world with no captain at the helm, no single country or region that calls the shots, and no single conception of order to provide stability," he writes. 

The United States “can neither cling futilely to the world that was, as Biden did, nor dismantle the old order and leave the United States and the rest of the world standing in the rubble, as Trump appears to be doing.”

In the book, Kupchan diagnoses the sources of global disarray and lays out his guide for building a new order fit for the emerging multipolar world. 

That mission must begin with the revival of American democracy and the nation’s steady leadership abroad, he argues.

"The United States and other democracies must first demonstrate that they can again deliver for their citizens and durably outperform illiberal and autocratic alternatives,” he writes. “Only then might the arc of history again bend toward democracy and justice."

"That world, ultimately, is the new that must be born.”

四家云厂商二季度一共花掉1651亿美元买设备、建机房，比一年前多出87%。

$SOXX却在10月22日一天跌了6.79%。

钱还在往产业链里砸，股价先跌了一大段。要看懂这种背离，得先把这笔钱流去了哪里画清楚。

二季度的现金资本开支：$AMZN 542亿美元，$GOOGL 449亿，$MSFT 358亿，$META 301亿。

Meta已经先交了三季度：资本开支（含融资租赁本金）349.1亿美元，经营现金流327.9亿，自由现金流变成负21.2亿。全年指引收窄到1350亿至1450亿美元。

赚来的现金，已经不够付这一季的建设账单。

这笔钱的流向，可以压成一条链：

云厂商 → 服务器整机 → GPU/ASIC → 代工、先进封装、HBM → 设备、EDA

链条旁边还有三条支线：网络交换、光模块、电力散热。

主链决定算力造不造得出来，支线决定造出来的算力能不能连起来、跑起来。

第一站是服务器整机。

鸿海、广达、$DELL、$SMCI 把GPU、内存、网卡和电源装进机柜。鸿海三季度营收3.03万亿新台币，环比增长20.44%。

这一环收入大、毛利薄，钱从这里过一手，大部分继续往上游走。

第二站是计算芯片，相当于数据中心的大脑。

$NVDA 截至7月的季度数据中心收入890亿美元，同比增长117%，其中直接来自超大规模云厂商的有487亿。

它卡住的是CUDA软件生态和整机柜系统。客户想换掉它，要重写软件、重新验证集群。

替代路线是定制ASIC。$AVGO 同期AI半导体收入167亿美元，同比增长221%，定制加速器占其中73%，客户包括谷歌TPU、OpenAI和Meta。$MRVL 走的是同一条路。

云厂商自己设计芯片，是为了压低每一次推理的成本，这部分钱会从GPU分流出去一块。

第三站是制造。

$TSM 三季度营收467.2亿美元，7纳米及以下先进制程占晶圆收入79%。不管GPU还是ASIC，最先进的那几代大多要回到台积电下单。

芯片造好以后还要做CoWoS先进封装，把计算芯片和HBM拼在同一块中介层上。这道工序过去两年一直是AI芯片出货的瓶颈之一，日月光和 $AMKR 在后段分担部分产能。

HBM是贴在计算芯片旁边的高速记忆。

计算再快，数据喂不进来也只能空转。

$MU 截至9月3日的季度营收542.3亿美元，一年前同期只有113.2亿。SK海力士二季度营业利润率达到76%。

亚马逊把2026年资本开支上调到约2200亿美元时，给出的原因是存储涨价。

云厂商多花的钱里，有一部分直接变成了存储厂的利润。

第四站是更上游的设备和设计工具。

$ASML 三季度收入116.6亿欧元，系统销售里逻辑占54%、存储占46%。公司说2027和2028年按现有计划的供给都无法完全满足需求，部分客户已经想下2029、2030年的订单。

$AMAT、$LRCX、$KLAC 分别守着沉积、刻蚀和检测量测。

$CDNS、$SNPS 的EDA软件和 $ARM 的架构授权，在芯片流片之前就先收钱。

三条支线同样在分钱。

网络交换把几万张卡连成一台机器。$ANET 做以太网交换机，$AVGO 三季度AI网络收入是一年前的2.5倍以上，$NVDA 自己也卖交换机，Spectrum-6已经支持共封装光学。

光模块把电信号转成光信号跑长距离，相当于机房里的神经。$LITE、$COHR 供应激光器和模块，$CRDO 做有源电缆和高速互联芯片，中际旭创是800G、1.6T光模块的主要供应商之一。

电力散热决定机房能不能通上电、会不会过热。$VRT 给出的三季度收入指引是36.5亿至38.5亿美元，有机增长34%至36%；$GEV、$ETN、$BE 分别对应发电设备、配电和现场供电。

正如9/25那条写的："公司可以讲故事，产业链很难一起配合演。"

这张地图的用处就在这里。云厂商资本开支一上调，台积电、海力士、ASML的数字应该跟着动；哪一环先停下来，往往比云厂商自己改口来得更早。

接下来几天的时间表：

美东10月27日晚8点（北京10月28日早8点），SK海力士三季度电话会。

美东10月28日盘前，$VRT 发布三季度业绩，11点电话会（北京23点）。

同一天下午2点（北京10月29日凌晨2点），美联储公布利率决议。

美东10月28日盘后，$GOOGL 下午4点半、$MSFT 下午5点半开电话会（北京10月29日凌晨4点半、5点半）。

美东10月29日下午5点（北京10月30日早5点），$AMZN 电话会。

要看三件事：全年和2027年资本开支有没有继续上调，云收入增速能不能盖住折旧，自由现金流还要被压多久。

这个系列会沿着这张图一环一环拆：GPU、定制ASIC、台积电代工、半导体设备、EDA与IP、存储与HBM、先进封装、服务器CPU、网络交换、光模块、服务器整机、电力散热，再回到云厂商的资本开支。

钱流得最快的环节，往往也是股价最先把预期打满的环节。

note_tweet.text:
1. Readers of this page know by now that JoyNews held a forum on Ghana's AI strategy and prospects. And the Digital Minister and I got into a serious debate about his Ministry's plan to build Ghana's competitor to Gemini, Kimi, ChatGPT, Qwen, Claude, etc.

2. Ghana's competitor to these global AI platforms is called GhanaChat.

3. It will be trained and hosted in a brand new AI datacenter.

4. 48 registries pooling data from across the public sector will make this AI smarter about Ghana than the foreign ones.

5. The AI datacenter and the "AI Fund" will cost about $270 million. Expect more to be spent on the registries and the apps. A lot of contracts. You can bet that a lot of ICT contractors are very happy.

6. The question is, if we have a couple of hundred million dollars to spend on making AI deliver great benefits for Ghana, should we spend it on GhanaChat, a top-tier AI data center, and the data-pooling system? And should we do it according to the strategy the Ministry has devised?

7. Or could we do much better by more critically assessing all our strategic options and comparing them to the Ministry's? 

8. My argument on the show was that I am not convinced about GhanaChat offering the best value for our money. 

9. It would take many pages to explain my position fully. But in this post I will highlight just the most important points.

10. Attached are extracts from page 13, 50, and 68 of Ghana's AI strategy.

11. If you have even the barest exposure to AI, you can see a massive error. Can you?

12. The target for how much computing capacity the country needs for next year (2027) is indicated as "1021 FLOPS" and the 2035 target as "1025 FLOPS".

13. If this was indeed correct, it would mean that the Ministry would like the entire computing capacity of the country in 2027 to be equivalent to a 1970s desktop computer. Or 2% of the capacity of the 1980 Intel math chip.

14. Howzat?

15. I'm sure you can agree that this would be totally ridiculous if that was the Ministry's intent. So, what happened?

16. Somebody who didn't fully understand how FLOPS work must have been involved in the drafting. What was meant to be 10 raised to the power 21 operations per second (10²¹ operations a second) was written out as "1021". Same for "1025". 

17. Why wasn't the error caught? Because in Ghana when doing "consultations", governments rarely engage independent and critical voices who will point out absurdities without fear of offending big men and women.

18. I am not being petty. There is a serious strategic confusion beyond mere typos.

19. Read properly as 10²¹ FLOPS, the Ministry is telling us that by next year it will have some 200,000 of Nvidia's newest chips in use in Ghana, 500 MW of power devoted to AI, all costing about US$24 billion (close to the Ghanaian government's entire programmed spending for 2026). 

20. The US$250 million AI datacenter now being procured supplies about 1% of this 2027 target.

21. Howzat?

22. Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision. Throughout the ministry's own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged.

23. My first major point here is that this is classic KATANOMICS: the lack of critical policy audiences. This is exactly how a sugar factory that was "designed from the start to fail" was allowed to be built. Many programs and initiatives in Ghana fail for precisely this absence of critical review.

24. In the strategy, you find statements like: "government aggressively building AI compute clusters" and by courting hyperscalers, "to leverage the scaling laws towards building general purpose AI and AGI". Then: "drastically increase Ghana's energy capacity 0.5 to 1 OOM per year". "OOM" means "order of magnitude".

25. When I challenged the Minister on TV, he confidently rebutted by claiming that the Energy Minister/Ministry has assured him of feasibility. Ghana's energy Ministry is committing to increase Ghana's power output by 3x to 10x EVERY YEAR so that the Digital Minister can deliver his AI strategy? Did anyone in Cabinet not protest that this projection in 8 years would mean expanding Ghana's electricity output by 10,000x?

26. I can bet you any amount that the Energy Minister will deny making any such commitments in Cabinet. Can we have clarity? Can JoyNews check?

27.  Page 68 of the strategy defines an "Artificial General Intelligence Lab" as "an AI lab with access to more than 1010 compute". No unit is given at all. In fact, as written it is totally meaningless. What they likely mean is that Ghana will support the establishment of a lab with computing capacity of 10¹⁰ FLOPS (10 gigaFLOPS).

28. The problem is that such a lab would be totally useless. To give you perspective, an iPhone 7 has about 350 gigaFLOPS of capacity.

29. What would be required to meet the Ministry's 2027 AI target? If for frontier model development, then the following spec would be reasonable: 400,000 16-bit Nvidia B300 GPU units, 1,114 MW of dedicated power (which is 26% of Ghana's peak demand). And the budget could easily hit US$47.2bn. For less frontier use, we can halve these numbers.

30. Counted in the 64-bit arithmetic that scientific supercomputers are ranked by, Ghana's 2027 target is 455 times the world's fastest machine, China's LineShine at 2.2 exaflops, and 53 times all 500 machines on the list combined.

31. Anyone with the barest exposure to Ghana's fiscal context can tell the Minister for free that this won't happen next year. 

32. Ghana's 2035 target of 10²⁵ is 160 times the entire global stock of AI compute today. Even if chips grow 1.4 times more energy-efficient every year, it would draw about 377 GW, 65 times Ghana's current installed generating capacity.

33. I will be charitable and propose that the strategy's drafters may have been thinking about training FLOP (note: without the "per second" at the end). For example, GPT-4's training run used about 2.1×10²⁵ FLOP, the same order of magnitude as Ghana's 2035 endpoint.

34. Unfortunately, that doesn't save the strategy. Recast this way, the target collapses the other way. 10²¹ FLOP is about 12 days' work for one H100 chip at 16-bit precision. 10²⁵ FLOP is one GPT-4-sized training run, which the US$250 million centre could finish in about four months. On that reading the centre meets the 2035 target before its first anniversary. Not meaningful.

35. Given how confusing the overall strategic plan is, would you bank on the first AI compute center and GhanaChat product already being procured at about $270 million? 

36. Here are some bare numbers: the budget, per our modelling, maps to about 2,100 GPUs and 4.3 MW of IT load. That alone adds the equivalent of 90% of Ghana's entire commercial data-centre load in 2024 (4.8 MW). Running it costs about US$76 million a year, which is about six times the revenue of the whole commercial industry.

37. A utilised GPU-hour costs about US$22 at base-case demand, against a market rate of US$6.71 today and roughly US$4.50 averaged over the hardware's life. The base case thus implies a subsidy of about US$61 million a year. 

38. If the concern is about Ministers and their Directors uploading sensitive documents into Gemini or Kimi, then why not a simpler sovereign AI assistant for the civil service first? 

39. That would need roughly 144 GPUs: about 7×10¹⁷ operations a second at 8-bit, US$13 million up front and US$6.7 million a year. That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy. Does Ghana really need to train its base model when orchestrators now allow one to host their own data and switch across multiple advanced open-weight models to serve an Assistant or Agentic system?

40. Howzat?

I’ve been looking into what @Kimi_Moonshot is building with Kimi K3.1 Pro, and the latest benchmark results caught my attention

With a 1M token context window, 2.8T total parameters and 104B active parameters, Kimi is targeting much more than everyday AI conversations

What I find interesting is its focus on practical work, from full project development in Unreal Engine, Unity and Godot to 3D modeling, CAD and financial analysis
